_nota: Initial answers to the five questions, now for Guasave, Sinaloa. They are starting hypotheses: each row is validated with a technician from the region. No local crop parameter is validated: there are only general FAO-56 coefficients. Same content and same keys as strategies.es.json.

labels.risks: What to check with your technician

E0.name: Maize → maize
E0.summary: What you do today: irrigated maize in the autumn-winter cycle, cycle after cycle.
E0.why: It is your current rotation. We compare it with the same yardstick as the other five.

evidence.detail: How green your plot is in each month of the year.
How much rain falls in your area each season.
Days of strong heat when maize flowers, in your area.

benefits: No change in seed, work or market.
You already know it and how your plot responds.
missing: How much irrigation water your plot uses each cycle.
Whether maize yields have dropped over the years.
risks: Whether reservoir water will last for the next cycle.
Pests and diseases that build up with maize year after year.

E1.name: Maize + cover crop → mulch → maize
E1.summary: A legume cover crop grows in relay and leaves mulch. Your technician picks the species.
E1.why: Covering the soil between cycles might protect it, although the cover crop also uses water.

evidence.detail: Months when your plot has no green plants.
Slope of the land, which speeds up running water.
Rain in past seasons, in your area.

benefits: It might protect the soil between cycles.
It might need less nitrogen fertilizer.
More organic matter over the years.
missing: How much extra water the cover crop uses.
How much nitrogen it adds on your plot.
risks: When to sow the relay without taking water from the maize.
Whether the cover species grows well in your area.
Dry mulch can raise the fire risk.

E2.name: Maize → beans → maize
E2.summary: One cycle of beans between two cycles of maize.
E2.why: Alternating crops spreads the risk, and beans add nitrogen to the soil.

evidence.detail: Water that beans need at each stage. These are general values, not for your area.
Rain in past seasons, in your area.

benefits: One more sale in the year.
Leaves nitrogen for the next maize.
Spreads the risk across two crops.
missing: The local price when you harvest.
How much irrigation water it needs compared with maize.
risks: Whitefly and virus.
Whether seed of the bean type your market buys is available.
Grain moisture at harvest.

E3.name: Maize → sorghum → maize
E3.summary: One cycle of sorghum between two cycles of maize.
E3.why: With little water to irrigate, a crop that needs less irrigation may be worth considering.

evidence.detail: How often rain is short at flowering, in your area.
Days of heat that damages the crop, in your area.
How it would do in a very dry season.

benefits: It might risk less of the harvest in a dry year.
The stalks can be used as fodder.
missing: Sorghum price and buyer in your area.
How many irrigations it needs in its cycle.
risks: Yellow sugarcane aphid.
Bird damage.
Whether its cycle matches the water available.

E4.name: Maize → chickpea → maize
E4.summary: One cycle of chickpea between two cycles of maize.
E4.why: It is a winter legume already grown in Sinaloa, and it adds nitrogen to the soil.

evidence.detail: Water that chickpea needs. We only have part of the general values.
Rain in past seasons, in your area.
Heat in past seasons, in your area.

benefits: Adds nitrogen to the soil, as a legume.
It might spread the risk across two crops.
missing: Its sowing dates and cycle in Guasave. Yield and price are for the municipality, not for your plot.
How many irrigations it needs on your plot.
risks: Which sowing dates fit the water available.
Where to get seed and who buys it.

E5.name: Maize → wheat → maize
E5.summary: One cycle of wheat between two cycles of maize.
E5.why: It is a winter cereal already grown in Sinaloa. It changes the crop while still harvesting grain.

evidence.detail: Water that wheat needs at each stage. These are general values, not for your area.
Rain in past seasons, in your area.
Heat in past seasons, in your area.

benefits: It might give one more sale in the year, if there is a buyer.
The stubble might leave cover on the soil.
missing: Its sowing dates and cycle in Guasave. Yield and price are for the municipality, not for your plot.
How many irrigations it needs on your plot.
risks: Whether machinery is needed to harvest it.
Where to get seed and who buys it.
Whether its cycle matches the water available.

E2.name: Maize → black bean → maize
E2.summary: One year of black bean between two years of maize.
missing: The local price when you harvest.
Yield of black bean on your soil.
risks: Planting date and days to harvest for black bean.
Whitefly and viruses.
Whether seed is available.
Grain moisture at harvest.

reasons.noMachinery: Without a tractor or hired service, harvesting {crop} by hand is not viable on this area.

rules.notAccepted: If you don't want to plant a crop, its option is left out.
rules.noMarket: With nowhere to sell, beans, chickpea, sorghum and wheat are left out.
rules.noMachinery: Without a tractor or hired service, sorghum and wheat are left out.
rules.nitrogen: Only legumes add nitrogen: beans and chickpea do; sorghum and wheat do not.

variantChosenBy.team: The kinilum team chose it for this illustrative case. On a real plot your technician chooses it.
